Commentary.Commentary: 217 needed then for India, to become the World Cup Champions amongst the Colts for the 4th time. Can Australia stop the Indian juggernaut? Join us back at 1800 local (0500 GMT) to find out.

Jonathan Merlo is giving an interview to Robert Key. He says that the pitch is good for both bat and ball. He says if you bowl well, it is difficult to score. But if you bat well you can score. Admits that there is a bit of turn on the surface which is a bit slow as well. Hopes that his spinners can do a good job. Is confident that if Australia bowl well, 216 can be defended.

Let us cast our minds back to 2012. It was the Under-19 World Cup final involving the same two teams - Australia and India. Then too, the Aussies batted first, posting a similar total - 225. It was thought to be a decent score but India chased it down pretty comfortably. Could be a similar case today. The difference between that Indian side and this one is that the 2018 unit looks prepared for all tests, the only thing being that it has not been tested so far.

India were brilliant with the ball but could have been much better. They were too short today and allowed the new batsmen to settle down comfortably. They focussed more on saving the boundaries than attacking the batsmen. Still, decent outing for all the bowlers with Porel, Shiva, Nagarkoti and Roy picking up 2 wickets each. Excellent team effort.

The surface is slow, no doubt but definitely not one which cannot give runs. The top order threw its wickets away while the middle order could not convert its starts. Only Jonathan Merlo played an innings of some substance, going deep till the 46th over. Had he departed early, the Aussies would not have even crossed 150. Remember, he was dropped on 0. The Indian side were generous on the field today, with 2 dropped catches and 3 missed run outs.

An under-par score from Australia. If truth be told, they are lucky to get to this total in the first place. India bowled well but they could have been better, had they adjusted their lines and lengths earlier.

OUT! Australia have been bowled out with 16 balls left. Criminal offense. Full and outside off, Hadley looks to drive but misses. The keeper appeals straightaway but the bowler is not that sure. Hadley starts to walk but then realizes that the umpire has not given it out. He now waits but then the umpire raises his finger! Nice acting by Hadley, showing a shocked look but well theatre perhaps is not the best need right now. INDIA NEED 217 FOR THE TITLE!
Full and outside off, Hadley gets across and then shoulders arms. Test match stuff. Nice poise.
Shivam Mavi is back on.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover. 2 runs and 2 wickets from the over. Nagarkoti's figures read 9-0-41-2.
Outside off, a feeble play and a miss, exposing all his three sticks.
Full and outside off, pushed past the bowler towards mid off.
Lloyd Pope is the last man in.

OUT! Number 9 is down! Seriously good work from India. A short ball outside off, Holt pulls i towards deep mid-wicket. Shiva Singh comes running in towards the ball for the catch but the ball lands short of him. It deflects away and the batsmen decide to go for the second. But Singh shows excellent awareness, quickly gets to the ball and returns a decent throw to the keeper. This time Harvik Desai does not try to be too fancy, quietly collects the ball and disturbs the bails. Holt dives in but way too late. Shiva Singh is already celebrating but the umpire still refers it upstairs. Replays only delay the inevitable.
Third umpire called in! Looks like an easy run out but the umpire has referred it upstairs...
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover for a single. Pretty decent defense for a number 10 batsman.
Ryan Hadley walks in at number 10, replacing Evans.
OUT! Brilliant bowling. Full and straight, Evans backs away and then looks to go inside out but misses. Timber. This might finish off quickly now.
Played to the point region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single. Gets off the mark, does Evans.
Oohhh... almost another one. Full and down the leg side, Evans looks to flick but gets a leading edge which does not carry to the bowler.

Landed on middle, Merlo looked to play the reverse sweep but go a top edge which went all the way to sweeper cover. Simple catch for Shiva Singh. Decent knock by Merlo, definitely not the quickest but from Australia's point of view, at least he has helped them get to a below par yet respectable total.

RUN OUT MISSED! Poor keeping. Holt works it through mid-wicket. The call is for two but the fielder quickly gets to the ball and returns a good throw to the keeper. But Harvik Desai, for some reason, leaps and then tries a back-flick. Misses the stumps. He could have just collected and then reached out. Holt was not even halfway.

DIRECT HIT WOULD HAVE HAD MERLO. Outside off, Holt plays it straight to backward point. The batsmen are not too sure about the single but eventually go for it. Anukul Sudhakar Roy takes his time, takes an aim and then has a shy at the striker's end but misses. Merlo was not even in the frame.

OUT! That is a super catch. He might have missed a couple today but this is a terrific take. The arm ball outside off, Sutherland looks to push it through the off side without moving his feet and gets a thick inside edge which goes right into the keeper's gloves! Very difficult catch because when the ball is coming off the inside edge, the keeper is blinded but he took it to perfection.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

Full and straight, watchfully blocked.

MISFIELD, FOUR! Sydney Harbour Bridge. Full and outside off, Sutherland reaches out and drives it through point. Riyan Parag gets across to his left from sweeper cover, is about to collect the ball but it goes right through his legs and to the fence behind. Did not even get his hands to it. His colleague in the dressing room cannot even bear to watch.

Outside off, punched straight to cover.
POWERPLAY 3 time. 5 fielders allowed outside the 30-yard circle, if Prithvi Shaw wishes.

Driven through the covers by the batsman.
Full and outside off, eased through the covers for a single.

OUT! Soft dismissal! Very important wicket again. Powerplay 3 is about to begin and this stand was about to reach the 50-mark. All set for a good platform to go big in the death. But Australia have been knocked back again by a wicket at a crucial juncture. Pretty similar to the way Param Uppal fell. Full and outside off, McSweeney looks to push it down the ground but ends up chipping it straight to Shiva who makes no mistake. The 49-run stand is broken and Australia find themselves in trouble again.
FOUR! Bad ball, full and down the leg side, McSweeney gets down and paddles it past short fine leg for a boundary.

TOP EDGE, SAFE! Very, very difficult chance. An excellent bouncer, outside off, McSweeney cannot resist himself and goes for the pull. But the bounce does him in and he gets a top edge. At first, it seems like an easy catch for the keeper as he gets across to his right. But then the ball swirls to his left, then right, then goes back and he has to run back too. Makes that late judgement and in the end, falls short of the ball even with a dive. Perhaps he got a glove to it. A single taken.

On a good length, pretty straight, tapped towards short mid-wicket for a quick one.
Outside off, this time Nathan opens the face of his bat and guides it through the vacant slip cordon to third man. This time that fielder has to run to his left. Just a run.

On a length outside off, McSweeney comes forward and gently opens the face of the bat to run the ball to third man for a single.
Shivam Mavi to bowl now.
Another arm ball - the third of this over - every alternate ball - whipped straight to square leg.

Another arm ball, pushed down to long on for one more.
Fuller on middle, pushed past the bowler towards long on for a run.

Time for some refreshments.

Sangha just follows it and ends up guiding it to the keeper behind who dives to his right and takes a decent catch. 52/1 has suddenly become 59/3 with the main run-getters dismissed.

Wrong end. Outside off, Sangha taps it to the off side and sets off for a quick single. Shivam Mavi gets to the ball but instead of an under-arm shy at the keeper's end, he picks the ball, turns around and then has a shy at the bowler's end by which time, Sangha makes it in. Now, by normal logic, if he had just under-armed at the striker's end, Merlo would have been a goner.
Double change. Kamlesh Nagarkoti to bowl as well.

DROPPED! Tough chance. Short and outside off, Merlo looks to cut but gets too close to the ball. Gets a thick outside edge which would have gone straight to first slip but by a regular keeper's habit, Harvik Desai goes for the catch. Unfortunately for him, he is unable to hang on.

The national anthems are done and dusted and we are ready to begin! Both teams are unchanged. The Aussie openers are out in the middle - Jack Edwards and Max Bryant. Shivam Mavi to start off proceedings with the first new ball. Edwards to face. Here we go...

TOSS - AUSTRALIA HAVE ELECTED TO BAT. Jason Sangha is quietly confident, stating that his team is far different from the one that lost its opener to India. Prithvi Shaw, too, wanted to bat first but is happy with the way the pitch is looking.
PITCH REPORT - The pitch looks a belter. Plus there is heavy breeze blowing which could aid shot-making towards the shorter side of the boundary.
WEATHER - It is slightly overcast at the moment but there is no threat of rain.

All set for the final game? Two of the best teams in the tournament have made it to the last game. India have been dominant and the standout favourites, while Australia have been improving after that first match drubbing. Which team will prevail today? Will India be unbeaten or can Australia avenge their defeat? Hello and a warm welcome to the final of the ICC Under-19 World Cup, 2018.
